out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Observed no written Employe Health Policy in place.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH THE FAIRFAX COUNTY EMPLOYEE ILLNESS AGREEMENT IN SPANISH AND IN ENGLISH. HAVE ALL EMPLOYEES READ AND SIGN A COPY. RETAIN ON SITE FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) Raw shelled eggs and Raw chicken were being stored above Ready-to-eat foods
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED THE RAW EGGS AND RAW CHICKEN THE RAW PROTEIN SHELF IN THE APPROPRIATE LOCATIONS.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: 1) observed cardboard being used as a shelf liner in the walk-in cooler. Cardboard was observed with dark colored mold on the corner
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. DISCARD ALL CARDBOARD LINERS. USE NONABSORBENT AND SMOOTH MATERIAL (ie: ACRYLIC, SHEET PAN) CAFE MONTMARTRE (Inspection Date: 06/04/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Premises Free of Unnecessary Items/Equipment
violations.observation: Observed that items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment are being stored on the premises in the kitchen, bar, and storage areas.
violations.corrective_action: Remove unnecessary items, including equipment which is no longer in use, from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. REMOVE ALL UNNECESSARY ITEMS TO PREVENT HARBORAGE CONDITIONS

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Observed one bottle of rodent repellent spray and one bottle of crawling insect insecticide in the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. PIC DISCARDED THE CHEMICALS. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO INCREASE SERVICES WITH A LICENSED PEST CONTROL OPERATOR. HOME-USE PESTICIDES ARE NOT ALLOW TO BE USED IN A PERMITTED FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) chicken stock was observed at 130f; 2) steak sauce was observed at 134f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC REHEATED THE SAUCE AND STOCK TO 165f ON THE STOVE. AFTER REHEATING, FOOD CAN BE HOT HELD AT 135f.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: homemade jam found in the walk-in cooler
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC DISCARDED THE JAM

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poisonous or Toxic Material
violations.observation: A container previously used to store liquid cleaning products being used to store house dressing.
violations.corrective_action: Do not store food in containers previously used to store poisonous or toxic materials. This practice may result in food contamination and subsequent medical consequences to anyone consuming the contaminated food. PIC DISCARDED THE BUCKET AND DRESSING. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO NOT USE CHEMICAL BUCKETS FOR FOOD STORAGE.

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: Observed allergy medicine being stored on a food preparation shelf.
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. PIC MOVED THE MEDICINE AWAY TO THE FIRST AID SECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed food being stored directly on the ground in the walk-in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PLEASE ELEVATE FOOD OFF THAT FLOOR. USE NSF APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS. CORRECT BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed cooking utensils being stored in a container of hot water. Water was observed at 130f.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC TOOK THE UTENSILS TO THE DISHWASHER TO BE WASHED AND SANITIZED. UTENSILS MAY BE STORED IN HOT WATER THAT IS 135f. CLEAN FREQUENTLY.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 1) 2DR prep top (salad) was observed at 58f; 2) 2DR prep top (grill) was observed at 49f
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC ADJUSTED THE TEMPERATURE OF THE SALAD COOLER. PIC MOVED ALL FOOD FROM THE BOTTOM OF THE COOLER TO THE WALK-IN. PIC PUT ALL THE FOOD IN THE TOP ON ICE. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO HAVE A SERVICE TECHNICIAN REPAIR THE COOLERS. COOLERS WORK BEST WHEN SET TO 32f-38f.

violations.title: Floors/Walls/Ceilings, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: Observed multiple ceiling tiles in the kitchen stained yellow.
violations.corrective_action: Floor, floor covering, walls, wall covering, and ceiling must be designed, constructed and installed to be smooth and easily cleanable. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC CLEAN CEILING TILES.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Approved Record Keeping, Tags/Labels
violations.observation: A record keeping system is not in place to maintain the tags of used/sold shellstock in chronological order correlated to the date that is recorded on the tag/label. EHS observed shell stock tags not being stored chronologically by date of last sale.
violations.corrective_action: Tags/labels must be maintained in chronological order by the date recorded on the tag/label when the last shellstock is used/sold. PIC reorganized tags so they are stored by date of last sale and agreed to keep them stored chronologically by date of last sale.

violations.title: Sanitizers, Criteria
violations.observation: The concentration of the @SANITIZER@ solution was measured at 200+ ppm. This concentration exceeds the approved limits for use with food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils in a foodservice establishment. EHS observed surface sanitizer being made at a concentration higher than 200+ppm.
violations.corrective_action: Maintain the concentration of @SANITIZER@ solution at @##@ppm. Verify concentration using the appropriate test kit. PIC diluted sanitizer to 100ppm using water
